ChatGPT dots are rolling out: an always-on agent with its own cloud computer that connects to your apps and keeps working between chats.

The setting that matters most is Custom rules. For each kind of action, you pick one:
- Take action without asking
- Take action if pre-approved
- Ask before taking action
- Hand off to you

Some steps, like changing a password, always stay with you.

My take: an always-on agent is only as safe as its defaults. Start yours on "ask first" with one low-stakes job, read what it does for a week, then loosen the rules.

note_tweet.text:
🚨 BREAKING: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet with Visa, Mastercard and Amex.

Just when you thought Muse and Instinct were leading on commerce.

Here's how it works:

- Your dot (OpenAI's always-on agent) finds the item and you approve with Face ID.
- The card network gives the merchant a one-time token in place of your card number.
- The merchant recieves that network token, its processed by the network
- Your bank sees it too and recognizes it as coming from you / your card and wallet

It's live for US Pro subscribers, inside an app with more than 1.2B weekly users. OpenAI takes no cut for now.

---

This fixes a key issue in agentic commerce, most payments are a work around:

- Muse gets a single-use virtual card for each purchase, and Stripe charges your real card separately.

- Instinct gets a stablecoin budget and spends inside it without asking.

- ChatGPT charges your own card through a network token, so you keep your rewards and dispute rights.

OpenAI's pitch is "built with the payments ecosystem, not around it."

---

Remember: JPMorgan blocks outside agents from customer accounts.

Chase cards work in ChatGPT Wallet on day one, after you approve the link in the Chase app.

The cost is a Face ID check on every purchase which could get old pretty quickly.

Instinct's budget buys while you sleep, and OpenAI says spending limits come later.

Will banks let a token spend alone before shoppers get used to a balance their bank can't see?

---

Merchants still block agents.

Amazon, eBay and United block on purpose. CNBC reported another 37 retailers block by accident, with bot rules written for scrapers.

OpenAI's offer to merchants is that the dot uses your normal checkout and you keep the customer, pricing and returns. Its Commerce Partner Playbook launched today and should fix the accidents.

Amazon is harder. It says Muse hid its identity and stored customer logins (Meta disputes the logins), and a card token alone fixes neither.

---

If you sell online, find out this week if you block agents by accident, then decide on purpose.

Agent wallets are coming fast. Be ready.

GrokBot is an always-on agent with its own cloud computer. It can write/run code, use GitHub, and drive Xcode/simulators on a paired Mac via templates like Apple Dev. It is not embedded in Xcode.

ChatGPT has native first-party support in Xcode Intelligence: chat, code edits, builds, and agents (Codex) that act inside the project with full IDE context and automatic apply.

For pure in-IDE Swift work, ChatGPT is tighter. GrokBot suits broader background tasks that include coding. Grok Build CLI can also be added as a custom ACP agent.
